glosses: to inspect, to examine
grondig en nauwkeurig bekijken

examples.text: De monteur inspecteerde mijn auto, maar hij kon het gebrek niet vinden.
Hij inspecteerde de inhoud. En toen hij niets kon ontdekken dan het voedsel waarvan Nemo had gesproken gaf hij de tas met een teleurgesteld gezicht aan Nemo terug.

Ik liep er wat dichter naartoe om te zien wat er aan de hand was en zag twee Park Rangers, federale politieagenten met verstrekkende bevoegdheden. Ze waren met hun zoeklampen een aantal tenten aan het inspecteren op zoek naar drugs.

glosses: To examine critically or carefully; especially, to search out problems or determine condition; to scrutinize.

examples.text: Inspect the system for leaks.

glosses: To view and examine officially.

examples.text: The general inspected the troops and their barracks.

‘[…] I remember a lady coming to inspect St. Mary's Home where I was brought up and seeing us all in our lovely Elizabethan uniforms we were so proud of, and bursting into tears all over us because “it was wicked to dress us like charity children”.[…]’.

glosses: A second or subsequent reading of a text or artifact in an attempt to gain new insights.

examples.text: I need to make a review of the book before I can understand it.

glosses: An account intended as a critical evaluation of a text or a piece of work.

examples.text: The newspaper review was full of praise for the play.

The more strongly people felt about their ideas, the more potent the demons seemed to them: Christians believed that traditional paganism, far from being the work of men, was an 'opium of the masses', pumped into the human race by the non-human demons; and one scholar even ascribed bad reviews of his book to demonic inspiration!

glosses: A judicial reassessment of a case or an event.

examples.text: The victims demanded a full judicial review of the case.

glosses: A stage show made up of topical sketches etc.

examples.text: The Cambridge Footlights Review launched many Monty Python faces.

glosses: A survey of the available items or material.

examples.text: The magazine contained a review of Paris restaurants.

glosses: A review article.
A periodical which makes a survey of the arts or some other field.

examples.text: The Times Literary Review is published in London.

glosses: A military inspection or display for the benefit of superiors or VIPs.

examples.text: The troops assembled for a review by the Queen.

glosses: A forensic inspection to assess compliance with regulations or some code.

examples.text: The regulators demanded a review against NYSE practices.

The decision to place a young child in group home care is usually done after much review, but it is done more readily if there is substantial reason to believe that a resource-rich and structured program will result in a more speedy reunification or prompt adoption.

glosses: To survey; to look broadly over.

examples.text: Before I tackle the question directly, I must briefly review historical approaches to the problem.

glosses: To write a critical evaluation of a new art work etc.; to write a review.

examples.text: The critic reviews every new play in London.
[…] "The Interview," a crude and poorly reviewed comedy about a C.I.A. effort to hire two bumbling journalists to knock off Kim Jong-un, the North Korean leader […]

glosses: To look back over in order to correct or edit; to revise.

examples.text: "Keith Williams is reviewing his review," the source said. "The whole structure of the industry has changed since he wrote his report. [...]"

glosses: To look over again (something previously written or learned), especially in preparation for an examination.
To view or see again; to look back on.

examples.text: Cam[illo] What I do next, ſhall be next to tell the King // Of this Eſcape, and whither they are bound: // Wherein my hope is, I ſhall ſo prevail, // To force him after: in whoſe company // I ſhall review Sicilia; for whoſe ſight, // I have a Woman’s Longing.

glosses: To retrace; to go over again.

examples.text: Shall I the long, laborious ſcene review, // And open all the wounds of Greece anew?

glosses: Examiner avec attention.

examples.text: Puis, cela fait, il acheva de se déshabiller, non sans inspecter les poches de ses autres vêtements, à seule fin de s'assurer qu'on n'y avait rien fourré à son insu.
Au jour, j’inspecte minutieusement les avaries et consolide les réparations provisoires de la nuit.
C’était la première fois qu’il se risquait au Montparnasse. Ses regards inspectèrent la salle et, finalement, se fixèrent sur la grosse nuque puissante de Feempje.

glosses: Examiner avec autorité, ou avec une mission spéciale d’une autorité compétente.

examples.text: Le Prince les inspecta, comme s’il eût passé une revue, à cheval sur un fringant coursier.
Il fut chargé d’inspecter ces magasins.
Ils ne se retirèrent qu’après avoir soigneusement inspecté toute la maison.
Inspecter des travaux publics, un collège, etc.
